why: A drove the real helper methods against the live Router and found two breakages that wrapping alone ships — the missing assistant function_call turn (400 on /v1/responses) and the streaming loop giving up on Router's role-only opening chunk, which silently killed every plugin reply — then fixed both and re-verified, while B ran simulator-only and asserts 'nothing the bot could do before has been lost', which is false for the plugin path on both default STREAM modes. On judgment A also measured rather than assumed: per-model price/latency on this bot's own three request shapes, a live cache-key A/B, and a reasoned refusal to enable fallbacks on a streaming chat bot — the exact lever B shipped as its headline branch on the strength of catalog prices alone.
A_best: Live, end-to-end exercise of the actual OpenAIHelper paths caught and fixed two plugin-path breakages (function_call history item; role-only stream chunk) that are genuine migration blockers, with before/after evidence and an OpenAI stand-in proving the provider path unchanged.
B_best: The unbuilt proposals show the best system-level framing in either report: billing users from Router's usage.cost instead of a 2023 flat TOKEN_PRICE, replacing the four hard-coded 2024 model tables with the live catalog, and porting the chat path to Responses natively so the levers stop being policy-file-only.
A_worst: The improvements don't compose cleanly — i1 and i2 both own router.policy.json and need a manual merge, i2 and i3 are mutually exclusive — and i3 changes the model behind every user-visible answer with nothing offline measuring quality, leaving real assembly and a product call on the CTO.
B_worst: Zero live verification (no key), so the plugin loop would have shipped broken in both streamed and buffered mode under a 'nothing lost' claim; and its flagship branch turns on cross-vendor fallbacks by default on all four features despite B itself noting fallbacks can't help the default streaming path and would silently change the bot's voice mid-conversation.
